That's the end of the match! Royal Challengers Bengaluru secure a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings. The frontline bowlers set the tone early, with Bhuvneshwar Kumar being the pick of the bowlers, picking up three wickets, and Jacob Duffy claiming two wickets, which put Chennai under immense pressure from the start. Later, Krunal Pandya and Abhinandan Singh joined the attack and added two more wickets to the tally. Chennai tried to fight back using all their weapons, with Sarfaraz Khan scoring a valiant 50 runs, Prashant Veer contributing 43, and Jamie Overton adding 37 runs, but it wasn't enough to chase the monumental target as RCB's bowlers maintained control throughout the innings. Tim David is the Player of the Match for his blistering innings.

The Mumbai Indians struggled in their chase of 151 runs, finishing well short at just 123 in 11 overs. The innings got off to a shaky start when Jofra Archer dismissed opener Rickelton early, putting immediate pressure on the batting side. Rohit Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav also fell quickly, leaving the top order in disarray. Although Tilak Varma and Naman Dhir showed some resistance, he was unable to convert his start into a match-defining performance. The middle overs proved to be decisive, as Ravi Bishnoi took two crucial wickets, removing key batters and putting an end to any hopes of a comeback. The lack of a substantial partnership significantly hindered Mumbai, as wickets continued to fall at regular intervals throughout the innings. Yashasvi Jaiswal is the Player of the Match.

The Gujarat Titans have closed their innings, setting a target of 211 runs. Jos Buttler shifted gears brilliantly during the powerplay, smashing 52 off just 27 balls. It was a top-class performance from Shubman Gill, who played a true captain's innings, scoring 70 runs. Meanwhile, Washington Sundar registered his maiden IPL fifty, scoring 55 and providing solid support at the other end. Glenn Phillips contributed a quick cameo, scoring 14 off 9 balls. On the bowling side, Delhi Capitals started positively but lost their momentum during the powerplay. Lungi Ngidi delivered an excellent performance, picking up the crucial wicket of Shubman Gill at a key stage. Mukesh Kumar claimed two wickets, while Kuldeep Yadav added one to his tally.  Can Delhi Capitals chase down this target, or will Gujarat Titans defend it? Stay tuned for the run chase.

Lucknow Super Giants snatch a memorable victory by three wickets. After losing both openers early, Ayush Badoni anchored the innings with a composed half-century, keeping the chase alive. The real star, however, was Mukul Choudhary, whose brilliant and unbeaten knock guided Lucknow to victory. His calm and calculated approach ensured that the chasing side never lost momentum, despite regular breakthroughs from the disciplined Kolkata bowlers. Vaibhav Arora and Anukul Roy claimed a couple of wickets each to make things tricky for the middle order, but it was Choudhary's class that proved decisive. Mukul Choudhary is the Player of the Match.

That's the end of the first innings. A big final over takes Royal Challengers Bengaluru past the 200 mark. Rajasthan Royals began really well with the ball, with five wickets in the first half of the innings but Bengaluru batters continued their aggressive approach to keep the runs flowing. Wickets kept falling at regular intervals, but skipper Rajat Patidar held firm at one end, anchoring the innings with a brilliant 63 and making a crucial impact in setting up this total, and Venkatesh Iyer did his impact role brilliantly. For the Rajasthan Royals, Jofra Archer, Ravi Bishnoi, and Brijesh Sharma picked up two wickets each. Can Rajasthan Royals chase this down, or will Royal Challengers Bengaluru successfully defend their total? Do join us for the run chase.

That's a comprehensive win for Rajasthan Royals, as they chase 202 with two overs to spare, winning by six wickets and remain unbeaten in the tournament. After the early departure of Yashasvi Jaiswal, the young Vaibhav Suryavanshi stepped up with a tremendous knock of 78 off just 26 balls, powering the chase and helping Rajasthan overhaul the target with ease, recording one of their highest Powerplay scores in the IPL. Dhruv Jurel played a composed hand, anchoring the innings beautifully and finishing unbeaten on 81. It was a tough outing for Royal Challengers Bengaluru bowlers, who looked largely ineffective as they were taken apart across the ground Josh Hazlewood and Krunal Pandya picked up two wickets each, but it wasn't enough to turn the tide. Vaibhav Suryavanshi is the Player of the Match.

column46: OUT! Caught. Anshul Kamboj to Lungi Ngidi. Length ball, wide outside off stump on the front foot Slog, thick edge in the air uncontrolled to short third man, caught by Singh. That is it. A clinical all-round performance from Chennai Super Kings as they register their first win of the tournament. Jamie Overton led the bowling attack brilliantly, picking up four wickets while conceding just 18 runs in his four overs. Anshul Kamboj also added three to his tally. Delhi Capitals got off to a promising start, but kept losing wickets at regular intervals, which derailed their chase. Tristan Stubbs showed great fight with a well-made 60, but his dismissal effectively sealed the game in CSK's favour. It is now back-to-back losses for Delhi Capitals, and they will need to regroup quickly going forward. Sanju Samson is the Player of the Match.

Lucknow Super Giants have posted a defendable total on the board. Aiden Markram provided a promising start with a brisk 30 off 21 deliveries, but his dismissal stalled the momentum at a crucial phase. From there on, the innings never quite recovered. The middle order struggled to build partnerships, and the scoring rate kept dipping under sustained pressure. It was a superb bowling effort led by Prasidh Krishna, who picked up a vital four-wicket haul, consistently breaking key stands and keeping the batters in check. Overall, a disciplined performance from the Gujarat side ensured they never allowed Lucknow to break free or build any meaningful momentum. Join us shortly for the run chase.

Gujarat Titans cruise to a comfortable seven-wicket victory. The openers laid a solid foundation, although Sai Sudharsan couldn't convert his start, falling for 15 off 14 deliveries. From there, it was all about composure and class. Shubman Gill and Jos Buttler stitched together a commanding partnership, both bringing up fluent half-centuries to put the chase firmly in control. Towards the finish, Washington Sundar and Rahul Tewatia added the finishing touches with positive intent. It was a tough outing for the Lucknow Super Giants bowlers, who struggled to break the key stand and couldn't stem the flow of runs once the partnership settled in. Prasidh Krishna is the Player of the Match.

Rickelton led the charge with his 81, while Rohit Sharma played his part with a fluent 78, setting the foundation for a comfortable finish. For the Kolkata Knight Riders, Sunil Narine, Vaibhav Arora, and Kartik Tyagi managed to pick up a wicket each, but it proved far from enough to stop a dominant Mumbai side. Shardul Thakur is the Player of the Match.

On the other hand, the Mumbai Indians will be disappointed with how they handled the innings. A comprehensive win for Sunrisers Hyderabad as they win by 57 runs. Two debutant fast bowlers shone for Sunrisers, Praful Hinge set the tone with a sensational three-wicket opening over that pushed Rajasthan Royals into deep trouble early, as they fell to 9-5 after three overs. Ravindra Jadeja and Donovan Ferreira fought back brilliantly with a superb 118-run stand for the sixth wicket to restore respectability, but after such a disastrous start, they were always behind in the chase. Sakib Hussain produced a beauty to dismiss Ferreira, and he joined Hinge in taking four wickets as Sunrisers closed out victory, the Royals bowled out an over short, despite some late hitting from Tushar Deshpande. Praful Hinge is the Player of the Match.

Chennai Super Kings register a convincing victory, winning by a healthy margin of runs. For the Kolkata Knight Riders, it was a tough chase right from the start as both openers fell inside the powerplay, leaving them on the back foot. Ajinkya Rahane and young Angkrish Raghuvanshi stitched together a 50-run stand, but neither could go on to make it count. Later, Rovman Powell and Ramandeep Singh added some valuable runs down the order, but all they managed to do was narrow the margin of defeat. For CSK, Noor Ahmad picked up three crucial wickets, and Anshul Kamboj picked up two. In the end, it's the Super Kings who walk away with the points, while the Knight Riders continue to search for their first win of the season. Noor Ahmad is the Player of the Match.

Virat Kohli set the tone early, anchoring the chase, and even after losing his opening partner in the powerplay he ensuring the momentum stayed with RCB. Skipper Rajat Patidar and Jitesh Sharma added the finishing touches with quick-fire knocks, guiding the team to victory with 4.5 overs to spare. It was a challenging outing for the Lucknow Super Giants bowlers, who put in a sincere effort, but the modest target proved insufficient to trouble a strong RCB batting lineup.

A brilliant century from Quinton de Kock has powered Mumbai Indians to an over par score of 195. Two early strikes gave the Kings the early advantage but de Kock and Naman Dhir built a magnificent century partnership. Dhir fell after completing his fifty, but de Kock, playing his first game of the season, continued to reach three figures, remaining unbeaten for his 112, including seven sixes. The Kings ended well after breaking the partnership, delivering a solid death bowling to squeeze the total under 200. Arshdeep Singh was at his very best today, picking up three wickets for just 22 runs. Marco Jansen and Shahshank Singh's overs were a crucial turning point for them. Join us for an interesting chase ahead.

Punjab Kings wrap up the chase in style, finishing the job with 3.3 overs to spare. Their batters showed clear intent from the outset, keeping the pressure firmly on the opposition. Prabhsimran Singh led the charge with a fluent 80, while Shreyas Iyer anchored the innings with a well-crafted 66. The duo built a superb partnership, accelerating the scoring and keeping the required rate comfortably in check. AM Ghazanfar, introduced as an impact player for Mumbai Indians, managed to pick up two wickets, but it wasn't enough to shift the momentum. With this convincing win, Punjab Kings climb to the top of the table and remain the only unbeaten side in the tournament. Arshdeep Singh is the Player of the Match for his brilliant spell.

That's the end of the first innings, and Kolkata Knight Riders have been restricted to 180. It was a brilliant start for the Titans as they picked up three quick wickets in no time, putting KKR under immediate pressure, but then a small yet important partnership between Rovman Powell and Cameron Green helped settle things for a while. However, the Titans' seamers kept things tight, striking at regular intervals and never allowing any real momentum to build. It was Cameron Green who stood tall for KKR, holding the innings together with a fighting 79, giving them something to defend in the end. Could this be a comfortable chase for the Titans? Gujarat Titans win by five wickets and complete a hat-trick of victories. The openers gave them a solid start in the chase, with Sai Sudharsan making a brisk 22 runs. Shubman Gill anchored the innings with a captain's knock of 86 runs, while Jos Buttler also chipped in with a useful 25 to guide Gujarat comfortably towards the target. For Kolkata Knight Riders, it's still a search for their first win of the season, and they'll be hoping for a strong comeback in their next outing. With the ball, Varun Chakaravarthy picked up two wickets, while Sunil Narine, Vaibhav Arora, and Ramandeep Singh claimed one wicket each. Shubman Gill is the Player of the Match.

That's the end of the first innings, a superb bowling effort from the Capitals as they've restricted RCB to 175! It was a flying start from the RCB openers, and Phil Salt carried that momentum beautifully with a well-made 63. Tim David played a quick cameo, but once he departed, the Capitals clawed their way back brilliantly. From there on, it was all control and discipline, never letting the batters settle, squeezing the scoring, and finishing the innings firmly on top. Can RCB fight back with the ball, or will the Capitals cruise to a comfortable victory? Stay tuned, we'll be back in a few minutes to find out!

David Miller finishes things off in style as the Delhi Capitals seal a six-wicket victory. After losing three quick wickets, KL Rahul and Tristan Stubbs stitched things together and steadied the innings. Rahul departed after a well-made 57, but Stubbs carried the momentum superbly, anchoring the chase with an unbeaten 60. Earlier, the RCB bowlers tightened the screws in the middle overs, with Bhuvneshwar Kumar leading the attack brilliantly to finish with three wickets. However, the crucial final over from Romario Shepherd proved costly, as Miller took charge at the death to snatch the win for Delhi. Tristan Stubbs is the Player of the Match.

That's a thrilling finish as Sunrisers Hyderabad clinch victory by 10 runs in a hard-fought contest. After losing Sanju Samson early, Ayush Mhatre and Ruturaj Gaikwad stitched together a quick 51 for the second wicket to keep the chase alive. Once they were dismissed, Matt Short tried to hold things together however the Sunrisers' bowlers kept hitting the right areas. They picked up wickets at regular intervals and never let CSK fully recover. Jamie Overton and Anshul Kamboj tried to drag Chennai Super Kings over the line with a late push, but a brilliant final over from Praful Hinge turned the game decisively, applying the brakes at the death and sealing it firmly in favour of Sunrisers Hyderabad.

Rajasthan Royals have posted a decent total on the board. Vaibhav Suryavanshi and Yashasvi Jaiswal got things off to a solid start, looking in good touch and making full use of the powerplay. Vaibhav Suryavanshi played a fine knock of 46, while Yashasvi Jaiswal provided good support with 39. On the other hand, Kolkata Knight Riders' bowlers pulled things back brilliantly. Kartik Tyagi and Varun Chakaravarthy were outstanding, picking up three wickets each and keeping the scoring in check. The run chase is coming up shortly.

Mumbai have posted a competitive total on the board. After losing both openers early, Naman Dhir played a composed and responsible knock, anchoring things nicely.  But the standout performer was undoubtedly Tilak Varma, with a superb unbeaten 101. He paced the innings beautifully and ensured Mumbai finished strongly. Gujarat Titans bowlers were disciplined for large parts of the innings, keeping things tight and striking at key intervals. However, they had no real answer to Tilak Varma's brilliance. Kagiso Rabada was the pick of the bowlers, finishing with three important wickets and leading the attack effectively. Join us shortly for the run chase.

Mumbai Indians register their second victory of the season with a clinical all-round performance, wrapping up a win by a massive 99 runs. The chase got off to a disastrous start as Sai Sudharsan fell on the very first delivery, instantly putting the Gujarat Titans under pressure. Shubman Gill tried to counterattack with a few fluent strokes, but couldn't convert his start into a substantial innings. However, wickets kept tumbling at the other end, never allowing momentum to build, Washinton Sundar's 26 the top score. The Mumbai bowling attack was relentless throughout, Ashwani Kumar led the way with his four-wicket haul, with support from Mitchell Santner and AM Ghanzanfar, all three, applying control and striking at crucial moments to choke the chase. Tilak Varma is the Player of the Match.

Rajasthan Royals seal a convincing win as they beat Lucknow Super Giants by 40 runs, the Super Giants bundled out for just 119 in 18 overs. A top-order collapse hurt them as three of the top four departed without scoring. Mitchell Marsh and Nicholas Pooran attempted to recover the chase, but slipped behind the required rate. Marsh top scored with a fighting 55 but there was little other support as wickets fell constantly. Jofra Archer starred with three wickets, well supported by Nadre Burger and Brijesh Sharma, who took two apiece, Rajasthan wrapping up a dominant performance to return to second in the table. Ravindra Jadeja is the Player of the Match.

Chennai Super Kings close their innings at 207 for 6, thanks to a masterclass from Sanju Samson, who played one of the finest knocks of the season. His unbeaten 101 off just 54 balls was the backbone of CSK's innings and ensured they posted a formidable total at Wankhede. Ruturaj Gaikwad's brisk 22 gave them a quick start, but wickets fell at regular intervals. Sarfaraz Khan, Shivam Dube, and Dewald Brevis all departed before they could convert their starts. The middle overs looked shaky, but Samson held firm, accelerating beautifully in the death overs. A late cameo from Jamie Overton added valuable runs before falling to Ashwani Kumar. For the Mumbai Indians, AM Ghazanfar and Ashwani Kumar picked up two wickets each. However, the likes of Hardik Pandya and Krish Bhagat were expensive, leaking runs at crucial stages. Chennai Super Kings beat Mumbai Indians by a huge margin of 103 runs, to register their third victory of the season so far. Facing a daunting target of 208, the chase never got going as they lost three wickets in as many overs, to be reeling at 11-3. The only real fight came from Suryakumar Yadav and Tilak Varma. They stitched together a partnership that gave Mumbai a glimmer of hope but with an ever increasing run-rate. Once they fell in quick succession there was no chance to recover. Akeal Hosein was the star, delivering a match-winning spell of 4 wickets for just 17 runs in his 4 overs, including a maiden. Sanju Samson is the Player of the Match for his tremendous batting performance.

Royal Challengers Bengaluru surge to second in the table with a commanding win. Gujarat Titans will rue an early missed opportunity as they dropped Virat Kohli on zero, and he made them pay with a superb 81, retaining the Orange Cap. Devdutt Padikkal provided excellent support, scoring a fluent 55 and setting the tone for the innings. Gujarat Titans managed to pick up a few wickets in the middle overs and briefly threatened a comeback, but the damage had already been done. This marks back-to-back losses for the Titans, and they'll need to regroup quickly to bounce back in the tournament. Virat Kohli is the Player of the Match.

A cakewalk of a chase for Sunrisers Hyderabad as they win by five wickets. After the early dismissal of Travis Head, Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan took charge. They attacked the bowlers all around the ground, with both bringing up fluent half-centuries to set the tone for the chase. Heinrich Klaasen and Nitish Kumar Reddy chipped in with handy cameos. The Rajasthan Royals bowlers struggled to find rhythm and couldn't pick up wickets at regular intervals, with Jofra Archer and Brijesh Sharma being the only bright spots, finishing with two wickets each. Ishan Kishan is the Player of the Match.

Chennai have posted a decent total on this pitch. It wasn't the smoothest of starts for CSK, as they lost three wickets inside the powerplay. Batting looked challenging on this surface, and the Gujarat bowlers kept things tight with disciplined line and length. Amid the early setbacks, Ruturaj Gaikwad stood tall, anchoring the innings with composure and guiding Chennai to a respectable total. His knock provided the stability CSK needed to recover. For Gujarat, the bowling attack was impressive. Kagiso Rabada showcased his class, striking at crucial moments and finishing with a brilliant three-wicket haul at an excellent economy rate. Do join us for the run chase.

Late contributions from the lower order ensured the chase stayed on track, finishing the game in the final over with just three wickets in hand. Cooper  Connolly is the Player of the Match for his brilliant performance.

A blazing start from the openers, who scored 129 runs in just 8.3 overs, put them in control early on. They guided their side home with ease and ensured Sunrisers maintain their strong momentum in the tournament. Heinrich Klaasen is the Player of the Match.

The Gujarat Titans successfully chase down the target inside 16 overs, winning by four wickets to close the gap on the playoff places. They appeared to be cruising after a strong start during the powerplay, Shubman Gill and Joss Buttler but impressive, but both fell before completing a half century. A wobble followed as they lost six wickets, but having got well ahead of the required rate, Rahul Tewatia guided them over the line with time to spare.  After an expensive start, the Royal Challengers Bengaluru bowlers performed well, but the target set was not sufficient to defend. The efforts of the RCB bowlers were commendable, and Bhuvneshwar Kumar stood out by taking three wickets. Jason Holder is the Player of the Match.

Rajasthan Royals have put up a mammoth total of 225 for 6 in their 20 overs, and it's been a fascinating innings with plenty of twists. Jaiswal and Suryavanshi fell cheaply inside the first two overs. Dhruv Jurel steadied things with a composed 42, but it was skipper Riyan Parag who truly set the tone. His 90 off 50 balls was a captain's knock. After Parag's dismissal, Donovan Ferreira lit up the death overs with a blistering 47 off just 14 balls. Mitchell Starc was the pick of the bowlers with 3 wickets, though he went for 40 runs. Axar Patel kept things relatively tight, while Jamieson and Natarajan were expensive. Delhi Capitals hunt down 226 with remarkable composure. Pathum Nissanka set the tone with a fluent 62 off 33 balls. His aggressive strokeplay ensured Delhi kept ahead of the asking rate right from the powerplay.  Lokesh Rahul was the anchor and aggressor rolled into one. He built partnerships with Nissanka and later Nitish Rana, ensuring the Capitals never lost momentum. Tristan Stubbs and Ashutosh Sharma calmly guided the chase home. Rajasthan's bowlers struggled to contain the flow, with Ravi Bishnoi and Nandre Burger particularly expensive. Even though Jadeja and Deshpande picked up wickets, Delhi's batting depth meant there was no collapse. With this win, Delhi Capitals break their jinx after the hat-trick of losses. Lokesh Rahul retained the orange cap and was rightfully adjudged as the Player of the Match.

Mumbai Indians finish their 20 overs at 159 for 7. A total that keeps them in the contest but feels slightly under par given the conditions. The innings began shakily with Will Jacks falling early, but Ryan Rickelton's aggressive 37 off 24 balls, featuring five sixes, gave them momentum. Naman Dhir was the standout, anchoring the middle overs with a composed yet attacking 57. Suryakumar Yadav added a quickfire 21 off 12. Hardik Pandya's slower 18 off 23 meant the finishing kick never arrived. A late cameo from Trent Boult lifted them past 150. With the ball, Anshul Kamboj's three wickets and Noor Ahmad's tight spell ensured Mumbai never broke free. Join us back for the run chase shortly.

Chennai Super Kings have chased down 160 in 18.1 overs, winning comfortably by 8 wickets. The chase began with Sanju Samson falling early to Jasprit Bumrah for 11, but that was the only real moment of concern. From there, Ruturaj Gaikwad led from the front with a captain's knock of 67 off 48, mixing patience with calculated aggression. He was well supported by Urvil Patel, who smashed 24 off just 12 balls. Kartik Sharma joined Gaikwad and played with composure, scoring 54 off 40, and together they stitched an unbeaten partnership that sealed the game. Bumrah was tidy with 1 for 20, but others leaked runs, especially Boult and Ghazanfar. Ruturaj Gaikwad is the Player of the Match.

KKR get it done comfortably and win by seven wickets. Ajinkya Rahane set the base with 43, Finn Allen chipped in with quick runs, and Angkrish Raghuvanshi's 59 kept the chase steady. Rinku Singh finished it off quickly with a short burst, with Cameron Green alongside him. For the opposition, Pat Cummins and Shivang Kumar picked up a wicket each but couldn't slow things down. Eshan Malinga was expensive, and the bowlers never really built pressure. Varun Chakaravarthy is the Player of the Match.

Punjab manage to post a decent total after their top order collapsed right at the start of the innings. Later, Suryansh Shedge and Marcus Stoinis steadied the innings with a crucial partnership in the middle overs, helping Punjab recover and put up a decent score. There was also a handy contribution from Marco Jansen in the death overs. It was a special moment for Shedge as he brought up his maiden IPL fifty. Gujarat Titans secure a four-wicket victory to maintain their fifth-place standing and continue their positive momentum. After the early dismissal of skipper Shubman Gill, the chase was expertly anchored by Sai Sudharsan, who ensured stability and kept the scoring rate in check while bringing up a well-crafted half-century. Later, Washington Sundar provided excellent support, guiding the team calmly to the finish line. For Punjab Kings, Arshdeep Singh and Vijaykumar Vyshak claimed two wickets each, but their efforts weren't enough as the team ended up on the losing side. Jason Holder is the Player of the Match.

LSG have wrapped up their innings with an imposing total on the board. Despite the early dismissal of Josh Inglis, the innings was brilliantly continued by Nicholas Pooran and Mitchell Marsh, who launched a fierce counterattack. The duo capitalised on the powerplay, stitching together a rapid 94-run partnership that put the Mumbai bowlers under immense pressure. As the innings progressed, Aiden Markram and Himmat Singh provided stability, building a composed partnership to ensure Lucknow finished strongly and posted a highly competitive target. It wasn't an easy outing for Mumbai's bowlers, especially early on, but they showed resilience by pulling things back in the middle and death overs. Regular wickets helped them stem the flow of runs and prevent the total from getting completely out of hand. Join us shortly for the second innings.

What a thrilling run chase from the Mumbai Indians as they hunt down a daunting 229 with remarkable authority, finishing with eight balls spare. The foundation was laid by a sensational opening stand between Rohit Sharma and Ryan Rickelton, both of whom dominated the powerplay and beyond with fearless strokeplay. Rickelton's explosive 83 off just 32 balls set the tone, while Rohit anchored the chase beautifully with a commanding 84, ensuring the required rate never spiralled out of control. Even as LSG fought back through Manimaran Siddharth and Mohammed Shami, picking up timely wickets, the momentum firmly stayed with MI.

A comfortable chase for the Chennai Super Kings as they win inside 18 overs with eight wickets in hand. It was a slow and steady start in the powerplay as they lost their skipper cheaply. Urvil Patel looked good for his brief stay, but the partnership between Sanju Samson and Kartik Sharma was the mainstay of the chase. Samson took the responsibility and played another magnificent match-winning knock this season, well supported by Sharma who flourished late in their unbroken century partnership. Delhi bowlers didn't have enough runs on the board to compete against some quality batting. Sanju Samson is the Player of the Match for his unbeaten 87 off 52 balls.

Sunrisers Hyderabad finish their innings with a commanding total of 235 for 4 in 20 overs. Abhishek Sharma gave them a flying start with 35 off just 13 balls, while Travis Head kept the momentum going with a brisk 38. The real damage came from Ishan Kishan and Heinrich Klaasen, who both got reprieves and made full use of that. Kishan's 55 set the platform, and Klaasen's 69 ensured the innings never lost steam. Nitish Kumar Reddy's cameo of 29 off 13 balls added the finishing touches, pushing the score well past the 200 mark. For Punjab Kings, the bowlers struggled to contain the flow of runs and their fielding worsened. Chahal was the most economical with figures of 1 for 32, while Arshdeep and Ferguson chipped in with a wicket each. Marco Jansen endured a tough outing, conceding 61 runs in his four overs. Stay tuned for the run chase.

Punjab Kings chase of 236 never quite found the rhythm they needed, despite a heroic effort from Cooper Connolly, who played a sensational knock of 107 off just 59 balls. Early wickets of Priyansh Arya, Prabhsimran Singh, and skipper Shreyas Iyer left them reeling at 23 for 3, and although Marcus Stoinis and Suryansh Shedge tried to rebuild, the pressure of the mounting run rate kept pulling them back. Connolly fought valiantly with clean hitting, but lacked consistent support from the other end. Sunrisers Hyderabad's bowlers struck at crucial intervals while Pat Cummins and Shivang Kumar led with two wickets each. In the end, Punjab Kings finished at 202 for 7, falling short by 33 runs, as Hyderabad sealed a commanding victory built on their strong batting display and disciplined bowling under pressure. Pat Cummins is the Player of the match.

Despite losing some early wickets, Delhi Capitals chase down the target comfortably with 2.5 overs to spare. Sameer Rizvi's responsible innings of 70 was well supported by Tristan Stubbs, who scored 39, to take their side over the line. Lucknow Super Giants tried hard to carry their early momentum, but they fell away sharply after the powerplay. Prince Yadav was the pick of the bowlers, picking up two wickets. Sameer Rizvi is the Player of the Match for his brilliant batting.

Tim David kept the hopes alive for his team with an aggressive cameo, but his innings eventually came to an end. Romario Shepherd struggled to connect the ball cleanly during the chase, while Krunal Pandya remained unbeaten on 28 runs. Finn Allen finishes it with a six to bring up his century. It was a remarkable all-round performance from KKR, having restricted Delhi to a below-par total, Allen's remarkable ton ensured they chased it with ease, inside of 15 overs. Two quick wickets in the powerplay gave the Capitals hope, but Cameron Green supported Allen with his 33, the partnership an unbroken century stand. Delhi bowlers couldn't defend the score because the target was not high enough. KKR climb above the Capitals up to the seventh position in the points table. Finn Allen is the Player of the Match.

Gujarat Titans win by 77 runs and move into second position on the table. Vaibhav Suryavanshi gave them a cracking start, but the pressure of the chase eventually led to a collapse, with the rest of the batting lineup failing to fire. Ravindra Jadeja tried to steady things, but he couldn't tilt the game in his side's favour. Gujarat Titans fast bowlers set the tone with disciplined spells. Kagiso Rabada picked up two wickets, whereas Jason Holder picked up two wickets. Rashid Khan then completely took control of the game with a match-winning four-wicket haul, sealing the contest for Gujarat Titans. Rashid Khan is the Player of the Match.

SIX! Anshul Kamboj to Shahbaz Ahmed. Full toss, wide outside off stump deep in crease Slog, well timed in the air under control over deep mid wicket for 6 runs. Lucknow Super Giants have posted 203 runs for the loss of eight wickets.
Mitchell Marsh and Josh Inglis gave their side a flying start in the power play. Especially Inglis, who took full control early on, smashing boundaries with ease and clearing the ropes regularly. He played a superb innings of 85 off just 33 balls. However, the middle and lower orders failed to support him, and the innings collapsed after the power play. Shahbaz Ahmed and Himmat Singh added a small but useful partnership for their side. Shahbaz Ahmed remained unbeaten on 43 off 25 balls, helping them to get to the 200 mark. For Chennai Super Kings, it was a strong comeback after the power play as they picked up wickets at regular intervals. Jamie Overton made a big impact with three wickets, while Noor Ahmad supported well from the other end with economical bowling and also picked up a wicket. Stay tuned for the run chase.

column46: SIX! Aiden Markram to Shivam Dube. Off break length ball, to leg on the front foot Slog, well timed in the air under control over deep mid wicket for 6 runs. Another maximum, and that seals the game! The ploy to rely on spin didn't work for Lucknow as Chennai successfully chased down the target. Urvil Patel's blistering knock made the chase look comfortable for CSK, as he posted the joint-fastest fifty in IPL history. Lucknow will be pleased with the way their bowlers fought back after Patel's explosive knock, but they will be disappointed with their fielding effort. Dropping crucial catches proved costly in the end, and that ultimately let them down in this contest. Shivam Dube and Prashant Veer then held their nerve, taking the game deep before guiding their team home in style. This is a crucial victory for CSK, and they will carry plenty of momentum from here. Jamie Overton is the Player of the Match.

Royal Challengers Bengaluru clinch a thrilling win by 2 wickets, successfully chasing down a target of 167 runs in a tense finish.
After a shaky start with early wickets of Virat Kohli and Devdutt Padikkal inside the powerplay, RCB found stability through Jacob Bethell and a counterattacking knock from Krunal Pandya, who top-scored with 73.
Despite regular breakthroughs from Corbin Bosch and tight spells from the bowling unit, RCB held their nerve in the final overs. Late contributions from Rasikh Salam and Bhuvneshwar Kumar guided them over the line in a tense finish with wickets in hand.

Punjab Kings have posted a competitive total on the board. Opener Priyansh Arya got them off to a flying start and brought up a well-compiled half-century. Skipper Shreyas Iyer then carried the momentum forward with a composed fifty of his own. Cooper Connolly chipped in with a handy cameo in the middle overs. For the Delhi Capitals, Mitchell Starc and Madhav Tiwari picked up two wickets each, though both were on the expensive side. Will Delhi Capitals chase down the target, or will Punjab Kings defend their total? Do join us for the run chase.

Delhi Capitals pulled off a thrilling three-wicket win in a high-pressure chase. After losing early wickets, skipper Axar Patel steadied the innings with a superb 56, shifting the momentum firmly in Delhi's favour. David Miller then kept the chase alive with a blazing 51, using his power-hitting to keep the required rate under control. Even after Miller's crucial dismissal, Ashutosh Sharma and Madhav Tiwari produced a quickfire cameo to apply the finishing touches and seal a memorable victory. Punjab Kings had made an excellent start with the ball, striking early to put Delhi under pressure. Arshdeep Singh was the standout performer, picking up two wickets while maintaining an impressive economy. However, the rest of the bowling attack struggled to contain the flow of runs, and that ultimately proved costly for Punjab. Player of the Match goes to Madhav Tiwari.

A dominant performance from the Gujarat Titans as they register a comprehensive 82-run victory over Sunrisers Hyderabad, to move top of the table. Defending their total with authority, the Titans' bowling attack completely dismantled the opposition, with Jason Holder and Kagiso Rabada starring with three wickets each, while Prasidh Krishna chipped in with a crucial two-wicket. Player of the Match goes to Kagiso Rabada.

Royal Challengers Bengaluru chase down 193 with composure, anchored by a masterful Virat Kohli, who struck 105 off 60 balls with calculated aggression. Despite the early loss of Jacob Bethell, Kohli's partnerships with Devdutt Padikkal ensured the asking rate never got out of control. Kartik Tyagi threatened with three breakthroughs. Kohli's dominance and a late cameo from Jitesh Sharma seal the chase in 19.1 overs, delivering RCB a convincing 6-wicket victory over KKR.

Tilak Varma finishes the match in style, his sixth six and a score of 75 to take Mumbai to victory. The chase started strongly with Ryan Rickelton making a quick 48, however after his dismissal wickets began to fall at regular intervals, placing them in a challenging position. Nonetheless, they managed to complete the chase thanks to valuable cameos from Rutherford and Jacks alongside Varma. In contrast the Punjab Kings bowlers will be disappointed in letting this one slip away after looking in control until late on.

column46: SIX! Anshul Kamboj to Nicholas Pooran. Reverse Swing-Out length ball, to leg on the front foot Slog, well timed in the air under control over long on for 6 runs. Lucknow Super Giants win by seven wickets! A dominant chase from the visitors as the openers set the tone with a blazing 135-run partnership, effectively taking the game away in the powerplay itself. Nicholas Pooran then finished the job in style with a fluent 32 off 17 balls, ensuring a comfortable finish to the chase. For Chennai Super Kings, the bowlers tried hard but were put under constant pressure throughout the innings. Spencer Johnson and Mukesh Choudhary picked up each a wicket, but CSK couldn't contain the flow of runs. A comprehensive win for LSG, though CSK remain in the playoff hunt mathematically and will need a strong finish from here on. Mitchell Marsh is the Player of the Match.
column99: Lucknow Super Giants win by 7 wickets

Travis Head and Abhishek Sharma gave their side a blazing start, combining for a fiery 82-run opening partnership. Both fell agonisingly short of their half-centuries but had already laid a solid foundation. Following the powerplay, SRH lost a few quick wickets, briefly slowing their momentum. However, Heinrich Klaasen and Nitish Kumar Reddy steadied the innings with a crucial partnership that kept the scoreboard ticking. Klaasen led the charge with a well-crafted 52, helping SRH surge past the 220-run mark. For Kolkata Knight Riders, Blessing Muzarabani was the standout performer with the ball, claiming four important wickets. Sunrisers Hyderabad seal a convincing 65-run victory with a strong all-round performance. Despite going for runs in the powerplay, their bowlers bounced back brilliantly to tighten control and restrict Kolkata Knight Riders. Finn Allen came out all guns blazing, but his early dismissal proved to be a turning point as Sunrisers Hyderabad seized momentum with disciplined bowling. Angkrish Raghuvanshi showed great composure in the middle, bringing up a fine half-century, but poor running between the wickets dented KKR's chase. For Sunrisers Hyderabad, Jaydev Unadkat starred with three wickets, while Eshan Malinga and Nitish Kumar Reddy chipped in with two each to wrap up a clinical win. Nitish Kumar Reddy is the Player of the Match.

That's the end of the first innings, and Rajasthan Royals have posted a solid total on the board. Despite losing Yashasvi Jaiswal early, Vaibhav Suryavanshi never allowed the bowlers to settle, smashing a quickfire 46. After his departure, Dhruv Jurel and the skipper, Riyan Parag, stitched together a crucial partnership to keep the Royals in a strong position. However, a late collapse cost them momentum and a potentially bigger score, thanks largely to Starc's game-changing spell that turned the tide in favour of the home side and earned him four wickets. Can Delhi Capitals chase this target and keep their playoff hopes alive? Let's find out.

Sunrisers Hyderabad complete the run chase to win by five wickets with an over to spare and take a big leap towards sealing a play-off place. Travis Head departed early, but Ishan Kishan, who scored 70, and Heinrich Klaasen, who made 47, played sensibly and guided the chase when it mattered most. The Chennai Super Kings bowlers tried hard to contain the flow of runs, but their efforts ultimately went in vain. Mukesh Choudhary was the pick of the bowlers with two wickets, but he received little support from the rest of the attack, allowing the Sunrisers Hyderabad batters to take control. The Player of the Match goes to Ishan Kishan.

A strong batting performance from Lucknow Super Giants sees them power over the 200 mark to post a total of 220. The openers providing an explosive start in a 100-run partnership inside the first eight overs. Mitchell Marsh played exceptionally well, maintaining a rapid pace on the scoreboard. Josh Inglis also delivered a sensational performance, while Rishabh Pant added valuable runs towards the end of the innings, despite Marsh falling just short of his century in the final over. The Rajasthan Royals bowlers struggled to take wickets at crucial moments, allowing the LSG batters to dominate throughout the innings. Yash Raj Punja managed to secure two wickets. Now, let's get ready for the chase!

A dominant all-round performance from Gujarat Titans sees them register a comfortable victory over Chennai Super Kings. Gujarat outplayed Chennai in every department and thoroughly deserved the win. Mohammed Siraj provided the perfect start with the ball, putting Chennai under pressure right from the beginning and almost sealing the game in the powerplay itself. Shivam Dube then produced a fiery counterattack with a quickfire 47 off just 17 balls, briefly giving CSK a glimmer of hope, but his innings ended with a stunning catch by Shubman Gill. Mohammed Siraj, Rashid Khan, and Kagiso Rabada starred with the ball, claiming three wickets each for Gujarat Titans. With this defeat, the playoff hopes and IPL 2026 campaign of Chennai Super Kings come to an end.

Sunrisers Hyderabad register a comfortable 55-run victory with a dominant all-round performance. Venkatesh Iyer gave the chase an aggressive start with a quickfire 44, while Rajat Patidar battled hard for his 56. Krunal Pandya also made a valuable contribution with 41 runs. Despite the defeat, Royal Challengers Bengaluru secured a top-two finish in the points table, as Sunrisers Hyderabad couldn't secure the required margin of victory to overhaul them. They will have to settle for third spot and a place in the Eliminator, whilst RCB will meet Gujarat Titans in Qualifier 1. Eshan Malinga led the bowling attack superbly with two wickets, while Sakib Hussain and Travis Head chipped in with a wicket each. Ishan Kisan is the Player of the Match.

A cakewalk victory for Punjab Kings as they win by seven wickets. After losing two early wickets, Prabhsimran Singh and Shreyas Iyer joined hands and added 140 runs for the third wicket. Rajasthan Royals secure their place in the playoffs as the fourth qualifying team with a clinical bowling performance. Jofra Archer starred with the ball, claiming three crucial wickets, while Nandre Burger, Brijesh Sharma and Yash Raj Punja chipped in with two wickets each to complete a dominant effort from the Royals' bowling attack. On the other hand, Mumbai Indians endured a disappointing season and will now look to regroup, make some important changes, and come back stronger next year with a fresh start.

That brings us to the end of the innings, with a big total of 209 for 5 on the board. Ayush Mhatre led the charge with a splendid 73 off just 43 deliveries, while Sarfaraz Khan provided late fireworks with a quick-fire 32 off 12 balls. Shivam Dube also added a composed 45 to cap off a dominant batting effort. Despite the total it was a decent effort from the Punjab Kings bowlers, with Vijaykumar Vyshak being the pick of the them, claiming two wickets. Xavier Bartlett, Marco Jansen, and Yuzvendra Chahal chipped in with a wicket each. A big chase awaits. Let's see how Punjab Kings approach this target. Join us shortly.

Punjab Kings seal a convincing five-wicket victory with eight balls to spare. Priyansh Arya set the tone early with a blistering 39 off just 11 deliveries, while Prabhsimran Singh and Cooper Connolly built on that momentum with solid contributions. Shreyas Iyer then led from the front, anchoring the chase with a brilliant half-century to guide his side home comfortably. Chennai Super Kings bowlers struggled to find their rhythm and leaked runs at crucial stages, which proved costly. Although Matt Henry and Anshul Kamboj picked up two wickets each, it wasn't enough to prevent the Punjab batting unit from completing a dominant chase. Priyansh Arya is the Player of the match for his early impact.

A strong comeback from the Delhi Capitals sees them seal a 40 run victory in the final match of the league phase for 2026. Kolkata Knight Riders were comfortably placed in the chase as long as skipper Ajinkya Rahane was at the crease. However, the turning point came when Kuldeep Yadav dismissed Rahane, triggering a collapse that allowed Delhi Capitals to seize control of the match. Kuldeep Yadav and Lungi Ngidi starred with the ball, picking up three wickets each, while Mitchell Starc chipped in with two wickets. Rahane fought a lone battle for KKR with a brilliant 63, but he couldn't take his side over the line. The earlier result had already seen Rajasthan Royals wrap up the final play-off place and end Kokata's hopes. The play-offs now await with the Royals joined by Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Gujarat Titans and Sunrisers Hyderabad who will fight it out for the crown. Kuldeep Yadav is the Player of the Match.

Rajasthan Royals have closed their first innings, setting a target of 211 for the Gujarat Titans. Yashasvi Jaiswal and Vaibhav Suryavanshi provided a strong start during the power play. Jaiswal scored 55 runs, while Suryavanshi smashed 31 off just 18 balls. Shimron Hetmyer chipped in with a quick cameo, and Dhruv Jurel played a superb knock of 75, anchoring a powerful performance for his side. It wasn't the best outing for the Gujarat Titans with the ball, as they struggled to contain the Rajasthan Royals batters. Kagiso Rabada picked up two wickets, while Rashid Khan, Ashok Sharma, Mohammed Siraj, and Prasidh Krishna took one wicket each. Stay tuned for the run chase.
